findings.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.java:79 — canView(client) short-circuits on global VIEW permission, bypassing client-specific denials and allowing administrators with global VIEW to read explicitly denied clients. Restrict the shortcut to built-in admin roles and evaluate fine-grained permissions against the target client.

ClientPermissionsV2.java:88 — canView() excludes global MANAGE permission, causing administrators with only global MANAGE to fail inherited client-scope list/view checks despite canView(ClientScopeModel) accepting that permission. Include MANAGE in the global read check.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.java:79 — canView(client) short-circuits on global VIEW permission, bypassing client-specific denials and allowing administrators with global VIEW to read explicitly denied clients. Restrict the shortcut to built-in admin roles and evaluate fine-grained permissions against the target client.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that canView(client) short-circuits on global VIEW permission, bypassing client-specific denials. Looking at the code in ClientPermissionsV2.java lines 77-82, canView(ClientModel client) first checks canView() (global) or canConfigure(client), and if either is true, returns true. Then it checks hasPermission(client, VIEW) for client-specific permission. This is the intended hierarchical permission model - if you have global VIEW permission, you can view all clients. The finding assumes there should be client-specific denial overrides, but this is not how the permission system is designed based on the diff. The code follows the same pattern as the parent class and other permission types (like UserPermissionsV2). There's no evidence in the diff that client-specific denials should override global permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.java:88 — canView() excludes global MANAGE permission, causing administrators with only global MANAGE to fail inherited client-scope list/view checks despite canView(ClientScopeModel) accepting that permission. Include MANAGE in the global read check.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, canView() at line 88 returns `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`. Meanwhile, canView(ClientScopeModel) at line 113 returns `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.VIEW_CLIENTS, AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The finding correctly identifies that canView() does not include MANAGE permission check, while canView(ClientScopeModel) does. This creates an inconsistency where a user with only global MANAGE permission would pass canView(ClientScopeModel) but fail canView(). Since canViewClientScopes() at line 68 returns canView(), and requireViewClientScopes() depends on canViewClientScopes(), this could cause administrators with global MANAGE permission to fail client-scope view checks unexpectedly.
